# Python Patterns

Curated by Skill Harbor: a complete idiom guide that makes Muse write and review Python the way experienced Python developers do. It covers the core principles first (readability counts, explicit over implicit, EAFP over look-before-you-leap), then modern type hints from basic annotations to Protocol-based duck typing and generics. Error handling gets specific exception catching and exception chaining instead of bare excepts. Context managers cover both the with statement and custom @contextmanager classes. Comprehensions and generators are presented with the rule for when a comprehension is too clever and should become a function. Data classes and NamedTuples, function and parameterized decorators, threading for I/O-bound work, multiprocessing for CPU-bound work, and async/await for concurrent I/O round out the skill, plus a standard src layout, a pyproject.toml with black/ruff/mypy/pytest presets, and a quick reference of Python idioms. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it is guidance, not a linter, so run black, ruff and mypy for real enforcement; some examples assume Python 3.9+ or 3.10+ features, check your version first. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
